questions.question: In OR Modelling, which description defines an undirected network?
options: A network whose edges carry no numerical values
A network whose edges have no prescribed orientation
A network in which every pair of vertices is joined
A network whose connections are pairs of opposite edges

questions.question: In an undirected network, an edge joins vertices $i$ and $j$. In which direction may it be traversed?
options: Only from $i$ to $j$, the order in which it is written
Either way, but with a different value in each direction
Neither way until an orientation has been chosen
From $i$ to $j$, and equally well from $j$ back to $i$

questions.question: An undirected edge between vertices $i$ and $j$ is written as the set $\{i,j\}$. What does this set notation express?
options: The edge runs from $i$ to $j$, as $i$ is listed first
$\{i,j\}$ and $\{j,i\}$ denote two distinct edges
The edge joins all vertices numbered from $i$ to $j$
Order is irrelevant: the sets $\{i,j\}$ and $\{j,i\}$ are equal

questions.question: Which connection is suitably modelled by an edge of an undirected network?
options: A one-way street leading from junction $P$ to junction $Q$
A cable linking two sites that carries data both ways
A pipe in which water runs only from tank 1 to tank 2
A rule that task $X$ must be finished before task $Y$ starts

questions.question: Ten two-way roads join pairs of towns. How many edges represent them in an undirected network, and how many in a directed network that allows the same travel?
options: 10 edges in both, since each road is one connection
20 edges in both, one per direction of travel
10 undirected edges, or 20 directed edges in total
10 undirected edges, or 10 directed edges in any orientation

questions.question: A server $S$ is linked by cables to computers $A$, $B$ and $C$, and data pass both ways along each cable. Which edge set models the cables in an undirected network?
Two-way roads join $A$ and $B$, and $B$ and $C$; they are the undirected edges $\{A,B\}$ and $\{B,C\}$. A driver at $C$ wants to reach $A$. What does the network allow?
options: No trip, since the edges are written from $A$ towards $C$
Driving from $C$ to $B$ and on to $A$ along these two edges
Only a direct trip, once an edge $\{C,A\}$ has been added
Driving from $C$ to $B$ only, since $\{A,B\}$ starts at $A$

questions.question: Travel times in minutes between towns are $t(P,Q)=4$, $t(Q,P)=6$, $t(Q,R)=3$ and $t(R,Q)=3$. Can they be modelled exactly by an undirected network with one time per edge?
options: No; edge $\{P,Q\}$ would need time 4 one way and 6 the other
Yes; give the edge $\{P,Q\}$ time 4 and the edge $\{Q,R\}$ time 3
Yes; give the edge $\{P,Q\}$ the average time of 5 minutes
No; the pair $Q,R$ appears twice, which is not allowed

questions.question: An undirected network has the edges $\{1,3\}$, $\{3,2\}$, $\{4,2\}$ and $\{3,5\}$. Which vertices share an edge with vertex 3?
options: 2 and 5 only
1 only
1, 2 and 5

questions.question: An undirected network has the edges $\{A,B\}$ of length 2, $\{B,C\}$ of length 5 and $\{A,C\}$ of length 4. What is the length of the trip from $C$ via $B$ to $A$?
In an undirected network, a route uses edges one after another, each in either direction. A route leads from $u$ to $v$. What follows about travel from $v$ to $u$?
options: A route exists only if each edge is listed twice
Nothing follows, just as in a one-way street network
A route exists, but it must use different edges
A route exists: the same edges in reverse order

questions.question: A town has several one-way streets among its two-way streets. Why is an undirected network with junctions as vertices not a suitable model of the town's streets?
options: It cannot carry street lengths as edge values
It would allow trips against the one-way streets
It requires every pair of junctions to be joined
It would forbid all trips along the one-way streets

questions.question: A network on vertices $1,\dots,n$ is stored as a table whose entry $(i,j)$ is 1 if one edge allows travel from $i$ to $j$ and 0 otherwise. Which property holds whenever the network is undirected?
options: Every diagonal entry $(i,i)$ is equal to 1
Entry $(i,j)$ always equals entry $(j,i)$
Every entry of the table is equal to 1
Entry $(i,j)$ is 1 exactly when $i<j$

questions.question: An undirected network on 5 vertices joins each pair of distinct vertices by at most one edge. What is the largest possible number of edges?

A directed network has the edges $A\to B$, $B\to A$, $B\to C$, $C\to D$, $D\to C$ and $A\to D$. All orientations are dropped and each joined pair becomes one undirected edge. How many edges does the undirected network have?
options: 6, one for each directed edge
2, only the pairs joined both ways
8, two for each joined pair
4, one for each joined pair

questions.question: A town has only the one-way streets $A\to B$, $C\to B$ and $C\to D$. All streets are made two-way, so the town becomes an undirected network. Which route then leads from $A$ to $D$?
options: $A\text{-}B\text{-}C\text{-}D$
$A\text{-}D$
$A\text{-}C\text{-}B\text{-}D$
$A\text{-}B\text{-}D$

questions.question: A road system with travel times is to be modelled exactly by an undirected network with one time per edge. Which condition on the roads is necessary and sufficient for this?
options: Every road is usable both ways, with equal time both ways
Every road is usable both ways, whatever the times
Every road takes the same time in each direction it allows
Every town can be reached from every other town

questions.question: In a network, a route uses edges one after another, each in a permitted direction. A student claims: if every vertex can reach every other vertex by a route, the network must be undirected. Which network refutes the claim?
options: Undirected edges $\{A,B\}$, $\{B,C\}$, $\{C,A\}$
Directed edges $A\to B$ and $B\to C$
Directed edges $A\to B$, $B\to C$, $C\to A$
Directed edges $A\to B$, $B\to A$, $B\to C$

questions.question: A network on vertices $1,2,3,4$ is stored as a table whose entry $(i,j)$ is 1 if one edge allows travel from $i$ to $j$ and 0 otherwise; all diagonal entries are 0. Exactly 7 entries of the table equal 1. What follows about the network?
options: It is not undirected, as undirected edges give an even count of 1-entries
It is undirected with 7 edges, since every entry equal to 1 is one edge
The table must contain an error, since 4 vertices allow at most 6 edges
It is undirected, since an entry equal to 1 joins its pair in both orders

questions.question: In an undirected network, a route uses edges one after another, each in either direction. Vertex $v$ can be reached from $u$, and also from $w$. What follows about $u$ and $w$?
options: Nothing, since both routes only end at the same vertex $v$
$w$ can be reached from $u$ only if $\{u,w\}$ is an edge
$w$ can be reached from $u$, via $v$ and the reversed route
$u$ can be reached from $w$, but not necessarily $w$ from $u$
